name: coremath_2_6
subject: Core Mathematics
substrand: Area of a Part of a Circle

conflicts.fact: Radius of the running Laikipia pivot / sector diagram in the cumulative model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 uses a pivot of r = 40 m (sector 120° ≈ 1675.52 m²) and the model adds the sector inside r = 40 m. Lesson 3's model step says the running Laikipia scenario has r = 21 m and θ = 90°, while its problems use 21 m at 120° and 28 m at 72°. The 'running' scenario changes.

conflicts.fact: Full-field radius of the Laikipia farm
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: title deed plot has radius 120 m (outer pipe 120 m, inner 80 m). Lesson 2: full circular field radius 40 m. Lesson 4: annulus r = 40 m, R = 70 m. Lesson 8: R = 45 m, r = 30 m. Lesson 6: plots 42 m and 35 m. The same farm/plot has incompatible dimensions.

conflicts.fact: Model diagram placement of sector: inside the inner circle vs relation to annulus
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 draws the 120° sector inside the inner circle (r = 40 m) on a diagram where the annulus is already labelled, while Lesson 4 treats the annular sector as the sector of the ring between r = 40 and R = 70 and as combining annulus and sector. Meanwhile Lesson 1's inner radius is 80 m, so the inner circle is inconsistent.

conflicts.fact: Segment area formula and angle definition
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5: A_segment = (θ/360)πr² − ½r²sinθ with θ the central angle. Lesson 6 states each lens segment area as (2θ/360)πr² − ½r²sin(2θ), using half-angle α, β, so θ means a different quantity; Lesson 8 says Q5 uses 2θ while listing the segment formula with θ.

Segment from circle A ≈ 485.8 m² and circle B ≈ 662.3 m² sum to 1148.1 m², which is consistent. However for angle 88.8° at r=42 m, the segment area is (88.8/360)π(42²) − ½(42²)sin88.8° ≈ 1367 − 881.7 ≈ 485.7, consistent; B: 114.2° at 35 m gives ≈ 1220.6 − 556.6... ≈ 664, roughly consistent.

conflicts.fact: Lesson sequence/coverage numbering: Lesson 3 (arc length) is omitted from test and Lesson 7 count
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 overview says 'Lesson 7 of 8' and 'five formulae' reference strip, but the sequence introduces sector, arc length, perimeter as well; Lesson 8's test covers lessons 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 only while the lesson 8 Explain refers to the 'annular sector of 1325.36 m²' for R=45, r=30, θ=135°, which computes to 1325.36 m² (correct).

conflicts.fact: Groups/predictions in Lesson 8: segment vs annular sector comparison
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 asks for the annular sector area to be compared with a segment for 'the same radius and angle', yet the annular sector depends on two radii, so the comparison is ill-defined relative to earlier definitions.
